main_text.p: operæ me pretium facturum existimo, si hanc quoque velut veram imaginem negociorum talium heic adscripsero, & oculis lectorum subjecero. Verba syn-graphæ Græca hæc sunt : Ἐ'δάνεισαν [?] Ἀ'νδροκλῆς Σφήττιος, ἐ Ναυκράτης Καρύστιος Ἀ'ρτέμωνι ἐ Ἀ'πολλοδώρᾳ Φασηλίτης, &c. VVolfius Latinè sic reddidit: Mutuarunt Androcles Sphet-tius & Naucrates Carystius Artemoni & Apollodoro Phaselitis argenti ter mille drachmas Athenis Menden usque, aut Scionem, & inde Bosporum. Quod si voluerint in finistrâ oram usque ad Borysthenem, & rursum Athenas, ducenis viceniis quinis millenas: sin post Arctiurum [?] solverint, è Ponto templum Argonautarum petituri, trecentis eas ter mille drachmas, vini amphoris Mendeis pignoris oppositis ter mille, quod evehetur Mendâ aut Scione, in navi xx remorum, quæ est Hyblesii navicularii. Oppigne-rant autem id vinum, non debentes pro-pterea cuiquam quicquam argenti, neque ad id mutuabuntur: & evehent merces, vini precio coemptas, rursus Athenas in eadem navi omnes. Perductis autem Athenas mercibus, reddent debitores creditoribus argentum, quantum debetur exsyngraphâ, intra vigesimum,

page.notes: Long s (s) in the Latin quotation and the Greek signature lines was rendered as plain s. The Greek lines are set on the line as printed; the first word and the Greek proper names are read from a small scan and should be checked against the original. "Arctiurum" is doubtful. The faint marks at the bottom right beside the signature are not legible and were not transcribed. The left edge of the scan shows fragments of the neighbouring page, which were left out.
